## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Asitābhūjātaka* (Ja 234) is a canonical Jātaka narrative included in the *Khuddakanikāya* of the Pali Tipiṭaka. The narrative opens in the present with the Buddha residing at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī, where he delivers the discourse in connection with a young woman (*aññataram kumārikam ārabbha*) [Fausböll 1879]. The verse text begins with the line *Tvam eva dānim akarā ti* [Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, the narrative concerns the royal daughter Asitābhū (*Asitābhu rājadhītā*) and a prince; in the resolution (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the ascetic of the past as himself, while the prince and princess are identified as the figures of the present narrative [Fausböll 1879].
